name: Hierarchical Clustering
description: Hierarchical clustering builds a tree of nested clusters (dendrogram) without requiring pre-specified number of clusters. It can be agglomerative (bottom-up: start with points, merge clusters) or divisive (top-down: start with one cluster, split recursively). Provides rich visualization through dendrograms.

concept.agglomerative: Bottom-up: each point starts as its own cluster, iteratively merge closest clusters
concept.divisive: Top-down: start with all points in one cluster, recursively split
concept.linkage: Method to measure distance between clusters
concept.dendrogram: Tree visualization showing cluster hierarchy and merge distances
concept.explanation: Creates a hierarchy where clusters at one level are nested within clusters at higher levels. Cut the dendrogram at desired height to get any number of clusters.

idealScenarios: When number of clusters is unknown

linkage.impact: Ward: minimizes variance; Complete: compact clusters; Single: chain-like

metric.impact: Must be compatible with linkage (Ward requires Euclidean)

nClusters.description: Number of clusters to extract (alternative to distance threshold)

distanceThreshold.description: Cut tree at this distance to get clusters

linkageMethods.ward: Minimizes variance within merged cluster (most common)
linkageMethods.single: Minimum distance between clusters (chaining effect, elongated clusters)

preprocessing: Consider dimensionality reduction for high-dim data
agglomerativeTraining: Start: each point is its own cluster (n clusters)
Compute distance matrix between all clusters
Merge closest pair of clusters based on linkage
extractingClusters: Use n_clusters parameter to cut dendrogram

complexity.timeTraining: O(n² × log(n)) to O(n³) depending on implementation
complexity.scalability: Poor for large n; use K-Means or DBSCAN for large datasets

pros: No need to specify number of clusters
Any number of clusters can be extracted post-hoc
cons: Different linkages give very different results

variants.divisive: Top-down splitting (less common, more computationally intensive)
variants.birch: Balanced Iterative Reducing and Clustering using Hierarchies - for large data
variants.optics: Ordering Points To Identify Clustering Structure - density-based hierarchical
